Asset type: canonical full-body character identity reference for Captain Harlan, Sylvia GM Severed Lands.
Primary request: Create ONE complete full-body illustration of Captain Harlan, 1024x1536 portrait orientation, with entire hair/hood, feet and equipment within comfortable inspection margins. Neutral near-front three-quarter standing pose; exactly one person, no portrait inset or additional figures.
Input roles: Image 1 is the accepted identity master. Isolate the CENTRE character only; it is the only identity source. Image 2 (Marla) governs anime drawing and selective painted finish ONLY; do not import her face, braid, apron or proportions into this character.
Authored facts: Harlan is a settled Human man, Thornwall guard captain, professional and conflicted after twenty years as a guard. He treats people courteously. Preserve the selected mature working adult appearance without adding a new injury.
Selected design: Copy the CENTRE full figure and face in image 1. Short tousled copper-red hair, strong mature clean-shaven face, light warm skin, green/grey eyes, practical navy quilted/studded long guard tunic, polished steel shoulder plates and forearm guards, muted red shoulder drape, brown belts, dark trousers and brown strapped boots. A sword stays sheathed at the same hip as in the reference. Keep the armour engraving, red cloth placement and outfit proportions recognisable. No helmet, extra weapons or new insignia.
Style and backdrop: retain the chosen design while drawing it in the accepted anime-fantasy finish; neutral charcoal ground, purposeful contours and readable local colours with controlled warm/cool light. Quiet reference pose, no scenery, action effects, text, labels, border, logo, new ornament or guessed hidden facts. All sides and equipment placement stay consistent with the master. Do not redesign, sexualise, de-age or glamourise the subject.
Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Asset type: square character portrait for Linden, Severed Lands.
Create ONE 1024x1024 square PNG, head-and-shoulders / upper-chest portrait of this exact selected individual, natural near-front three-quarter view. Highest hair/headwear near 12% of image height, eyes around 40%, chin around 63%, modest background around the whole head. All hair, headwear and crown inside the raw square. Clothing fills the lower area; no hands, book, lantern, basket, bow or message in the face area. A downstream adjustable crop gives the tighter circular head view.
Image 1 is the full-body IDENTITY MASTER and image 2 is its checked multiview reference. Preserve exact face structure, age, build, complexion, hair/headwear, scars, expression and visible outfit. Image 3 is Marla for drawn anime contour/shadow/material finish ONLY, not her face, hair, braid, forelock, pose or costume.
Authored facts: Senior Riftborn Door researcher using they/them, from an academic home world. Eight years studying the dormant Door, documented its first violet flicker, obsessive and sleep-deprived, filling an eighteenth notebook. No revealed biological ancestry, new magic or invented instrument power.
Selected appearance: A tall slender Riftborn adult of androgynous appearance with pale olive skin, a long narrow oval face, tired blue-green eyes and thin round steel spectacles. Straight ash-blond chin-length hair is tucked behind ordinary rounded ears and gathered at the nape. Cream work coat over a russet sleeveless wrap vest, loose grey trousers, plain belt and dark ankle boots. One closed slate-blue notebook under the left arm and a short charcoal pencil in the right hand. Intent sleep-deprived bearing, without assigned ancestry or magical powers.
 
Simple charcoal backdrop, controlled light, distinct local colours. Preserve an expressive anime-drawn face with deliberate lids/brows/mouth and economical age lines appropriate to this subject; no photoreal pores, chibi, 3D render or generic same-face replacement. No new marks, emblems, powers, labels, letters, border, logo or other person.
Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

prompt_set.full_body:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: Severed Lands shared character catalogue. Create ONE full-body character reference, portrait orientation 1024x1536. The sole input image is rendering STYLE ONLY; its person, face, hair, pale forelock, braid, clothes and pose must not transfer. Establish this fresh subject from the authored facts and new design below. No older subject art is an input.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Authored facts:
Settled Human man, independent Warrens fence, nervous meticulous and discreet, keeps sellers buyers and storage private. Do not depict identifiable stolen artifacts or disclose an unknown object.

Fresh visual design:
A short slight middle-aged man with pale sallow skin, a narrow pointed face, fine mouth, large watchful grey eyes behind small thin round spectacles and discreet fine lines at the eyes. Thin straight ash-brown hair neatly side-parted, receding slightly, clean-shaven. A plain dull umber short coat over a blue-grey high-neck tunic, dark brown straight trousers and modest dark boots. Small dark closed document pouch tucked at his RIGHT waist; no displayed merchandise or weapons. Both empty hands clasped low in front, shoulders slightly drawn in, nervous attentive expression without comic caricature. No uniform, bright insignia, royal status, literal drum, stolen object, occult eye motif or benchmark braid/forelock.

Show the ENTIRE figure from hair top to boot soles, with 7 percent comfortable clear margin above and below, both hands and any held object fully inside frame. Relaxed near-front three-quarter pose, plainly readable costume topology and gear sides. Neutral dark charcoal background, subtle grounding shadow, warm directional edge light with readable local colors. Clear anime-designed eyes, face contours and large shadow shapes, painted textile/material finish; no photorealistic face or skin pores. No environment, extra figure, decorative border, text, lettering or UI. Do not draw a portrait crop or cut off the legs.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Medium worm-like ambush predator of Warden ruins, exceptional stonework camouflage, attacks with beak and tentacles. No invented eyes or legs; lingering Rift-burn is not an external spell effect.

Restrained violet and blue-green reflections within those seams, no large neon halo. Preserve a coherent worm silhouette rather than loose disembodied tentacles. prompt_set.full_body:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: complete Severed Lands creature reference. Make ONE PORTRAIT 1024x1536 image. The sole input is RENDERING STYLE ONLY, not subject identity, human anatomy, hair, clothing, pose or facial marks. Establish a fresh default from the authored facts below; no earlier subject art is an input.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Medium undead Rift Echo of predation, a life-draining death-memory in a humanoid form. Its authored lore and Bite text differ about spawn formation; depict neither formation mechanism and add no biography, noble title or faction.

One lean adult male-presenting humanoid undead with pale ash-olive skin, a long angular face, deep-set pale grey eyes, straight nose and long black hair combed back to the nape without a forelock or braid. A controlled predatory half smile shows just two dry upper fangs, no blood. Practical ankle-length charcoal wool coat with a high plain collar over a folded dark burgundy tunic, narrow black belt, fitted dark trousers and worn dark closed boots. Both hands visible and empty with exactly five long fingers each, no jewelry or weapon. Rift distortion is part of his Echo material: at the temples, throat and hand edges, opaque skin planes branch into nested bevels that appear to continue deeper than the single surface, with restrained cold opal/violet reflections in the recesses. No wound, stone statue, exposed organ, extra physical face, head or limb. Keep one coherent humanoid silhouette, two arms, two legs and one head. No aristocratic insignia, cape shaped like bat wings, victim, blood pool, literal spawn birth, modern cyberpunk suit or copied Marla outfit.

Show the COMPLETE figure/form from highest point to feet or connected base, with comfortable clear margins around every extremity and prop. Use a neutral dark charcoal background, subtle grounding shadow and controlled warm edge/cool interior light. # The Cartographer

The Cartographer maintains the Scavenger's Compact most valuable asset — a living map of the Hollows, updated weekly with route changes, phasing patterns, and hazard reports from Compact members. They've been doing this for fifteen years. No one knows their real name. No one knows what they look like under the hood they always wear.

The Cartographer is said to be a former Athenaeum scholar, expelled for reasons they won't discuss. Their cartographic skill is undeniable — the map is the most accurate navigational tool in the Severed Lands, more reliable than anything the Athenaeum or the Returners have produced. The Cartographer doesn't charge for access. The map belongs to the Compact. The Compact belongs to the scavengers.

Recently, the map has been wrong. Routes that should be stable are phasing unpredictably. Landmarks are moving. The Cartographer has been working around the clock to keep up. They're not sleeping. They're barely eating. Something about the Hollows has changed, and the Cartographer is trying to map a city that no longer wants to be mapped.

## Personality

The Cartographer is obsessive, brilliant, and terrified. The map has been their life's work. Watching it become unreliable is like watching a language lose its grammar. They communicate through notes slipped under doors. They never meet anyone in person. Their handwriting has gotten shakier.

## Appearance and artwork

An anonymous adult cartographer fully concealed in a worn charcoal hooded travelling robe and simple layered dark cloth. Deep opaque shadow hides the entire face from every angle; no visible eyes, skin, hair, ears, facial features or species cues. Plain dark gloves, practical dark covered footwear, a rolled parchment map, a small leather document satchel and a simple brass divider. A slightly stooped, exhausted, guarded posture. No revealed identity, gender, species, tattoos, insignia or magical effects.

This prepared appearance is an editable visual default; the character's authored identity, mechanics and lore above remain authoritative.

name: "Captain Harlan"
role: "Thornwall guard captain"
disposition: "Neutral (institutional)"
species: "Human (settled)"
location: "Thornwall"
---

# Captain Harlan

Captain Harlan commands the Thornwall guard — the men and women who keep order in the market, enforce the council's policies, and very pointedly do not patrol the Warrens. He's been a guard for twenty years, captain for five. He's good at the job. He's not sure he likes it anymore.

Harlan enforces policies he didn't write. The Riftborn registration requirements were Lord Voss's idea. The travel restrictions were Voss's idea. Harlan enforces them because it's his job, not because he believes in them. He's seen Riftborn who are more settled than some of the market's human vendors. He's also seen Rift surges coincide with Riftborn arrivals. He doesn't know what the truth is. His job doesn't require him to know. It requires him to keep order.

Harlan is the council's instrument. He's aware of this. It bothers him more than it used to.

## Personality

Harlan is professional, conflicted, and increasingly uncomfortable with his role. He treats Riftborn registrants with more courtesy than policy requires — a small resistance, but a real one. He's not a reformer. He's not ready to defy orders. But he's listening.

## Appearance and artwork

A broad-shouldered adult Human man in his early fifties with weathered medium fair skin, brown eyes, short dark hair graying at the temples, a neatly trimmed salt-and-pepper beard and a square tired face. Practical worn steel breastplate over a muted blue-gray guard tunic, plain dark shoulder cloak, leather gloves, dark trousers and brown boots. A sheathed service sword and an ordinary belt pouch. Head uncovered, calm professional but troubled expression.

# V

V is the oldest known Riftborn — a figure who arrived through the Rift decades ago and has been searching for a way back ever since. Unlike most Riftborn, V retained memories of their original world: a place V describes only as "green" and "quiet" and "gone." Those three words are the most personal information V has ever shared about themself.

V founded the Returners not as an army but as a support network — Riftborn helping Riftborn, pooling knowledge and resources toward a shared goal. Over the decades, the Returners grew into something larger: a research organization, a political force, and the closest thing the Severed Lands has to a Riftborn advocacy group. V didn't plan any of that. V just kept working, and people kept joining.

V is rarely at Waystation. They spend most of their time in the field — tracking leads on Warden fragments, investigating the two unaccounted-for Doors, following Rift surge patterns that might reveal something about the Doors' decline. When V returns, decisions get made. When V is gone, the senior Returners keep things running.

## Personality

V is patient, methodical, and carrying the weight of decades. They don't inspire through charisma — they inspire through competence. Every Returner knows that V has given their entire life to this mission. That kind of commitment is hard to argue with, and V rarely needs to argue.

V is not cold, but they are guarded. They've lost too many people — Returners who died on patrol, Riftborn who gave up and left, friends who became Hollowed and stopped recognizing them. V doesn't form new attachments easily. When they do, it's significant.

V's defining trait is patience bordering on obsession. They've been working on the Door problem for longer than most Returners have been alive. They believe the answer exists — in a Warden inscription they haven't found yet, in a Door fragment they haven't recovered, in a surge pattern they haven't mapped. The belief is not faith. It's the conclusion of decades of evidence. V is not guessing. V is waiting.

## Role in a Campaign

**As ally:** V is the quest-giver, the mentor, the voice of experience. They send the party after Warden fragments, Door leads, and Rift surge data. They provide context, resources, and the occasional warning that goes unheeded until it's too late.

**As antagonist:** V's patience has a dark side. If the party discovers a way to force the Door open — a method V considers too dangerous, too uncertain, too likely to bring something through first — V will oppose them. Not with violence. V doesn't do violence. But with obstruction, with withheld information, with the full weight of the Returners' loyalty. The party wants to force the Door. V has spent decades trying to open it safely. Neither side is wrong. The conflict writes itself.

**As mystery:** V knows more than they share. About their home world. About the Wardens. About what they've seen in the deep Cairnfields and the unaccounted-for Door sites. A campaign that earns V's trust might eventually learn the full story. A campaign that doesn't might never know what V was really looking for.

## Behind the Screen

V's true nature is left deliberately ambiguous. Possible truths include:

- V is exactly what they appear to be: a Riftborn who remembers home and wants to return.
- V was part of the Wardens — not metaphorically, literally. V's "decades" of searching might be centuries. The Wardens' symbol — a circle bisected by a line — appears in V's personal notes.
- V knows why the Doors are dying. They're not trying to open the Door. They're trying to prevent something from coming through.
- V's home world was destroyed by whatever created the Rift. V isn't trying to go home. V is trying to make sure it doesn't happen here.

The truth is for the DM to decide. The ambiguity is the point.

# Tessa

Tessa runs the best bakery in Thornwall. Her bread is the reason the morning market has a line before sunrise. She's been baking since she could reach the oven — her mother ran the bakery before her, and her grandmother before that. The recipes haven't changed in three generations. The quality hasn't either.

Tessa doesn't care about Riftborn politics. She cares about flour prices. The council's grain tariffs — controlled by House Voss — directly affect her margins. She's been quietly vocal about this at market gatherings. "Quietly vocal" in Thornwall means she says things that sound like complaints about the weather but everyone knows are complaints about Lord Voss.

She'll sell to anyone. She'll also slip an extra roll to the Warrens kids who hang around the market at closing time. She doesn't make a thing of it. The rolls just happen to be "leftover."

## Personality

Warm, practical, and politically aware in the way that small business owners have to be. Tessa treats baking as craft and community — the bakery feeds Thornwall, and Thornwall takes care of the bakery. That's how it's always worked. She doesn't see why Riftborn should be any different.

Quiet, dutiful, and carrying a private grief. Miri does her job. She doesn't make waves. She just makes sure the Gate is slightly less terrifying than it could be.

# Auntie Salt

Auntie Salt runs the Warrens' information network — a web of barkeeps, merchants, street kids, and domestic servants who feed her everything they see and hear. She's the Warrens Court's intelligence arm, but she's not loyal to the Court. She's loyal to the information trade, and she sells to anyone who can pay.

Salt has no territory and no gang. Her currency is knowledge, and she's the richest person in the Warrens — not in gold, but in leverage. She knows about Kael's daughter. She knows about Trask's Nexus negotiations. She knows which Warrens resident has been cultivating a Rift pool in their basement. She's known that last one for weeks. She hasn't told anyone yet. She's waiting for the right buyer.

Salt's network extends beyond the Warrens — she has informants in Thornwall proper, in the Hollows Crews, and (rumor has it) in the Athenaeum. The extent of her reach is unknown. The accuracy of her information is frighteningly consistent.

## Personality

Salt is cheerful, grandmotherly, and utterly amoral about the information trade. She treats secrets like produce — some are fresh, some are past their sell-by date, all of them have a price. She genuinely likes people. She just likes knowing things about them more. She keeps a pot of tea going at all hours. Visitors are always offered a cup. No one knows if the tea is safe. Everyone drinks it anyway.

# Fume

Fume sells alchemical supplies in the Crossroads market — reagents and the occasional Rift-touched compound that the Athenaeum would classify as hazardous. He arrived through the Rift with a case of alchemical formulas and the burns to prove he'd tested most of them. His stall smells of sulfur and something sweeter that lingers in the sinuses.

Hollows scavengers buy his glow-paste — a compound that emits light for hours without heat, essential for navigating the ruins without attracting riftbeasts. The Athenaeum buys his more exotic compounds through intermediaries. Fume doesn't ask what they're for. He just provides the materials.

# The Cartographer

The Cartographer maintains the Scavenger's Compact most valuable asset — a living map of the Hollows, updated weekly with route changes, phasing patterns, and hazard reports from Compact members. They've been doing this for fifteen years. No one knows their real name. No one knows what they look like under the hood they always wear.

The Cartographer is said to be a former Athenaeum scholar, expelled for reasons they won't discuss. Their cartographic skill is undeniable — the map is the most accurate navigational tool in the Severed Lands, more reliable than anything the Athenaeum or the Returners have produced. The Cartographer doesn't charge for access. The map belongs to the Compact. The Compact belongs to the scavengers.

Recently, the map has been wrong. Routes that should be stable are phasing unpredictably. Landmarks are moving. The Cartographer has been working around the clock to keep up. They're not sleeping. They're barely eating. Something about the Hollows has changed, and the Cartographer is trying to map a city that no longer wants to be mapped.

## Personality

The Cartographer is obsessive, brilliant, and terrified. The map has been their life's work. Watching it become unreliable is like watching a language lose its grammar. They communicate through notes slipped under doors. They never meet anyone in person. Their handwriting has gotten shakier.

# Captain Harlan

Captain Harlan commands the Thornwall guard — the men and women who keep order in the market, enforce the council's policies, and very pointedly do not patrol the Warrens. He's been a guard for twenty years, captain for five. He's good at the job. He's not sure he likes it anymore.

# V

V is the oldest known Riftborn — a figure who arrived through the Rift decades ago and has been searching for a way back ever since. Unlike most Riftborn, V retained memories of their original world: a place V describes only as "green" and "quiet" and "gone." Those three words are the most personal information V has ever shared about themself.

V founded the Returners not as an army but as a support network — Riftborn helping Riftborn, pooling knowledge and resources toward a shared goal. Over the decades, the Returners grew into something larger: a research organization, a political force, and the closest thing the Severed Lands has to a Riftborn advocacy group. V didn't plan any of that. V just kept working, and people kept joining.

V is rarely at Waystation. They spend most of their time in the field — tracking leads on Warden fragments, investigating the two unaccounted-for Doors, following Rift surge patterns that might reveal something about the Doors' decline. When V returns, decisions get made. When V is gone, the senior Returners keep things running.

## Personality

V is patient, methodical, and carrying the weight of decades. They don't inspire through charisma — they inspire through competence. Every Returner knows that V has given their entire life to this mission. That kind of commitment is hard to argue with, and V rarely needs to argue.

V is not cold, but they are guarded. They've lost too many people — Returners who died on patrol, Riftborn who gave up and left, friends who became Hollowed and stopped recognizing them. V doesn't form new attachments easily. When they do, it's significant.

V's defining trait is patience bordering on obsession. They've been working on the Door problem for longer than most Returners have been alive. They believe the answer exists — in a Warden inscription they haven't found yet, in a Door fragment they haven't recovered, in a surge pattern they haven't mapped. The belief is not faith. It's the conclusion of decades of evidence. V is not guessing. V is waiting.

## Role in a Campaign

**As ally:** V is the quest-giver, the mentor, the voice of experience. They send the party after Warden fragments, Door leads, and Rift surge data. They provide context, resources, and the occasional warning that goes unheeded until it's too late.

**As antagonist:** V's patience has a dark side. If the party discovers a way to force the Door open — a method V considers too dangerous, too uncertain, too likely to bring something through first — V will oppose them. Not with violence. V doesn't do violence. But with obstruction, with withheld information, with the full weight of the Returners' loyalty. The party wants to force the Door. V has spent decades trying to open it safely. Neither side is wrong. The conflict writes itself.

**As mystery:** V knows more than they share. About their home world. About the Wardens. About what they've seen in the deep Cairnfields and the unaccounted-for Door sites. A campaign that earns V's trust might eventually learn the full story. A campaign that doesn't might never know what V was really looking for.

## Behind the Screen

V's true nature is left deliberately ambiguous. Possible truths include:

- V is exactly what they appear to be: a Riftborn who remembers home and wants to return.
- V was part of the Wardens — not metaphorically, literally. V's "decades" of searching might be centuries. The Wardens' symbol — a circle bisected by a line — appears in V's personal notes.
- V knows why the Doors are dying. They're not trying to open the Door. They're trying to prevent something from coming through.
- V's home world was destroyed by whatever created the Rift. V isn't trying to go home. V is trying to make sure it doesn't happen here.

The truth is for the DM to decide. The ambiguity is the point.

A mature humanlike androgynous adult Riftborn field researcher with olive-gold skin, grey-green eyes, short wavy dark-indigo hair and a pale cream forelock, small plain ear studs, and a lean medium-height build. A pearl half-cape with green lining and fine woven trim covers layered indigo and forest-green scholar travel clothes, loose indigo trousers and brown lace-up boots. A closed brown folio is held against the torso; a small brown field pouch hangs at the belt. Patient, methodical, guarded competence and quiet attentive authority. Use they/them pronouns. # The Quartermaster

The Quartermaster runs Waystation's supplies, equipment, and armory. They're a Riftborn from a world of endless war — they arrived with a soldier's discipline and a logistical mind that's kept the Returners functioning through decades of scarcity. They don't talk about their home world. They don't need to. The way they handle weapons tells you everything.

Every piece of equipment at Waystation passes through the Quartermaster's hands. They know what's in the armory, what's overdue for maintenance, what was checked out and never returned. They're the reason Returner patrols are equipped and fed. They're the reason the signal tower has replacement mirrors. They're the reason Waystation's supplies lasted through the last winter, barely, and they'll be the reason it lasts through the next one, or it won't, and either way the Quartermaster will have done everything possible.

## Personality

The Quartermaster is efficient, unsentimental, and capable of identifying any weapon by weight alone. They treat supplies as a moral responsibility — every ration shorted is a patrol that goes hungry. They don't socialize. They don't need to. The armory is their domain, and they keep it like a temple.

## Hook

Equipment has been going missing from the armory — small items, impossible to trace, but the Quartermaster notices everything. Someone in Waystation is stockpiling. The Quartermaster suspects the Radicals. They're building a case. They need someone to help them prove it — someone who isn't a Returner, who doesn't have loyalties the Quartermaster can't predict.

# Old Crane

Old Crane is the oldest living practitioner of the Veiled Path — a monk who's been living at the Spire, the tallest pillar in the Cairnfields, for longer than anyone can verify. He claims sixty years. He looks older. Some of his stories reference events that happened eighty years ago. When asked about the discrepancy, he says the Veil confuses time. He says it with the kind of casual certainty that's hard to argue with.

Crane no longer trains students. He lives at the Spire in solitude, trading information for supplies with Returner patrols and the occasional brave scavenger. He knows the Cairnfields better than anyone — every pillar, every pool, every riftbeast territory. He's seen things in the Veil that he won't describe. Crane's body has been partially transformed by decades of phase-stepping — his movements are slightly out of sync with his physical position, like a video that's a frame behind. His voice echoes even when there's nothing to echo off. He's more Veil than flesh at this point. He seems fine with it.

Crane is signaling Waystation — three mirrored flashes, the emergency code. He hasn't signaled in years. The last time he did, a Rift surge reshaped the eastern Cairnfields. Whatever he's seen from the Spire, it's worse.

# Iro

Iro is a Rift Seeker — a descendant of the Rift Raiders who rejected the martial code and sought inner stillness instead. He's been wandering the Cairnfields for fifteen years, mastering the discipline that his ancestors considered cowardice. He's not a coward. He's just decided that the Eternal Battle his people believe in isn't a war. It's the struggle to stay calm in a world that wants you to fight.

Iro occasionally serves as a translator between the Raiders and outsiders — one of the few people who speaks both Rift-tongue and Common, and the only one the Raiders will tolerate. He doesn't enjoy it. Translating for Korr means listening to Korr's plans and being unable to warn anyone. Translating for Vex means standing in silence for hours while she writes orders that will get people killed. The Seeker's discipline is non-interference. The discipline is very hard to maintain.

## Personality

Iro is calm, melancholy, and carrying the weight of his people's choices. He loves the Raiders. They're his family, his heritage, his blood. He also believes they're wrong — about the Eternal Battle, about violence as purpose, about everything. He can't change them. He can barely stand to watch. But he stays, because someone has to speak for them, and he's the only one who can.

# Tessa

Tessa runs the best bakery in Thornwall. Her bread is the reason the morning market has a line before sunrise. She's been baking since she could reach the oven — her mother ran the bakery before her, and her grandmother before that. The recipes haven't changed in three generations. The quality hasn't either.

She's been quietly vocal about this at market gatherings. "Quietly vocal" in Thornwall means she says things that sound like complaints about the weather but everyone knows are complaints about Lord Voss.

She'll sell to anyone. She'll also slip an extra roll to the Warrens kids who hang around the market at closing time. She doesn't make a thing of it. The rolls just happen to be "leftover."

## Personality

Warm, practical, and politically aware in the way that small business owners have to be. Tessa treats baking as craft and community — the bakery feeds Thornwall, and Thornwall takes care of the bakery. That's how it's always worked. She doesn't see why Riftborn should be any different.

Rigg is an independent scavenger — no crew affiliation, no Compact membership, no backup. He's been working the Hollows for a decade and he's still alive, which is either skill or luck or a combination he doesn't examine too closely. He specializes in the smaller finds — Warden fragments embedded in walls, pre-Rift coins, the kind of salvage that doesn't attract crew attention.

# Kit

Kit is twelve years old and knows the Warrens better than anyone except Grim. They're second-generation Riftborn — their parents arrived through the Rift before Kit was born. Kit has never known any world but the Warrens. They've never needed to.

Kit works as an informant for Auntie Salt — running messages, watching doors, reporting who comes and goes. They're paid in food, coin, and the protection that comes from being useful to someone powerful. Kit doesn't think of it as spying. It's just what you do to survive in the Warrens.

Kit knows every Warrens resident by sight. They know who's new, who's sick, who's been asking questions about the Returners, who's been asking questions about the Radicals. They don't understand the politics. They understand that information has value, and they're very good at collecting it.

## Personality

Smart, watchful, and old before their time. Kit doesn't act like a child because the Warrens doesn't let children act like children. They're friendly in a guarded way — they'll talk to anyone, but they're always evaluating. Auntie Salt taught them that.

# Lorn

Lorn hunts riftbeasts for a living. Not for sport, not for vengeance — for money. Every major settlement posts bounties on dangerous riftbeasts, and Lorn collects. They've been hunting for ten years. They've killed more riftbeasts than most patrols. They've got the scars to prove it and the coin to show for it.

Lorn works alone. They've tried partners. The partners died. Lorn doesn't talk about that.

Their knowledge of riftbeast behavior is encyclopedic — they know pack patterns, hunting cycles, pool preferences, the subtle signs that an area is claimed territory. They share this knowledge with Returner patrols when they cross paths. They don't charge for the information. They consider it professional courtesy.

## Personality

Lorn is quiet, solitary, and carrying the weight of every partner they've lost. They treat hunting as a profession rather than a calling — it's dangerous work, but it's honest work, and someone has to do it. They're very good at it. They wish they didn't have to be.

# Auntie Salt

Auntie Salt runs the Warrens' information network — a web of barkeeps, merchants, street kids, and domestic servants who feed her everything they see and hear. She's the Warrens Court's intelligence arm, but she's not loyal to the Court. She's loyal to the information trade, and she sells to anyone who can pay.

Salt has no territory and no gang. Her currency is knowledge, and she's the richest person in the Warrens — not in gold, but in leverage. She knows about Kael's daughter. She knows about Trask's Nexus negotiations. She knows which Warrens resident has been cultivating a Rift pool in their basement. She's known that last one for weeks. She hasn't told anyone yet. She's waiting for the right buyer.

Salt's network extends beyond the Warrens — she has informants in Thornwall proper, in the Hollows Crews, and (rumor has it) in the Athenaeum. The extent of her reach is unknown. The accuracy of her information is frighteningly consistent.

## Personality

Salt is cheerful, grandmotherly, and utterly amoral about the information trade. She treats secrets like produce — some are fresh, some are past their sell-by date, all of them have a price. She genuinely likes people. She just likes knowing things about them more. She keeps a pot of tea going at all hours. Visitors are always offered a cup. No one knows if the tea is safe. Everyone drinks it anyway.

Fume sells alchemical supplies in the Crossroads market — reagents and the occasional Rift-touched compound that the Athenaeum would classify as hazardous. Hollows scavengers buy his glow-paste — a compound that emits light for hours without heat, essential for navigating the ruins without attracting riftbeasts. The Athenaeum buys his more exotic compounds through intermediaries. Fume doesn't ask what they're for. He just provides the materials.

# Saffron

Saffron runs a herbalist stall in the Thornwall market by day and a free clinic in the Warrens by night. She's settled — born in Thornwall, never been through the Rift — but she's spent enough time in the Warrens to know that the council's policies are killing people. She doesn't make a political statement about it. She just keeps showing up with medicine.

Her knowledge of Rift-touched conditions is largely self-taught — the Athenaeum's medical texts don't cover Warrens-level care, and Saffron has had to figure out on her own what helps and what makes things worse. She's made mistakes. She's learned from them. She's saved more lives than Thornwall's official healers.

## Personality

Saffron is tired, compassionate, and quietly furious at the system she works within. She doesn't waste energy on anger. She uses it on patients. Her hands are steady. Her diagnostic eye is sharp. Her supply of Rift-burn salve is always running low.

# The Lace Brothers

The Lace Brothers are three Riftborn siblings who run the Warrens' smuggling operation. Thread, Hook, and Needle — names they chose themselves, the origin of which they've never explained. They specialize in contraband the Thornwall Council has banned: unsanctioned Warden fragments, Rift-touched curios, information that would get someone killed if it reached the right ears.

They're the Warrens' primary link to the Hollows Crews — every crew that pulls something valuable out of the ruins eventually does business with the Lace Brothers. They're also the primary fence for the Caravan Jackals, which the Court officially doesn't know about and unofficially profits from.

The Brothers are ambitious, young, and already eyeing Madame Thistle's territory. When Thistle dies — and she is dying — the succession fight will be between the Brothers and Thistle's lieutenants. The Brothers have been preparing. They've been stockpiling funds, building alliances, and making the kind of promises that are very hard to break.

## Personality

The Brothers present a unified front but have distinct personalities: Thread is the negotiator — smooth, charming, always smiling. Hook is the enforcer — quiet, watchful, never more than arm's reach from a weapon. Needle is the logistics mind — the one who knows where everything is, who owes what, whose shipment is late. They finish each other's sentences. It's unsettling.

## Hook

The Brothers have acquired something unusual — a Warden artifact that's fully intact, not fragmentary. They're not sure what it does. They're auctioning it to the highest bidder. The Returners, House Kael, and the Unbound are all bidding. The Brothers are drawing out the auction. They're enjoying the attention.

# Drum

Drum is a fence — he buys scavenged goods from independent scavengers who don't want to deal with the Lace Brothers' commission rates. His operation is smaller, quieter, and considerably less legal than the Brothers'. The Court tolerates him because he handles the volume they don't want. The council doesn't know he exists. Drum prefers it that way.

Drum's specialty is items that are too hot for the regular market — artifacts with identifiable origins, goods that "fell off a caravan," information that would start a war if it reached the wrong faction. He doesn't ask where things come from. He doesn't share who he sells to. His operation is built on the principle that the less you know, the less you can be forced to reveal.

## Personality

Drum is nervous, meticulous, and very good at staying invisible. He treats fencing as a risk management profession — every transaction is calculated, every buyer is vetted, every item is stored in a different location. He's been doing this for years. He's never been caught. He intends to keep it that way.

Echo is a bard of the College of Echoes — a subclass that channels fragments of lost worlds through song. Their performances aren't entertainment. They're remembrance. When Echo sings, the audience hears snatches of music from home worlds they can't return to, melodies from places that might not exist anymore, harmonies that feel like memory even to people who remember nothing.

Echo travels between settlements — Waystation, Thornwall, Nexus, the smaller villages that the Guild caravans serve. They perform in taverns and market squares, never charging, never staying long. People who hear Echo's songs sometimes cry without knowing why. Sometimes they remember things they'd forgotten. Sometimes they ask Echo to stop. Echo always stops.

retained_styles.name: Severed Lands — Dark heroic fantasy
retained_styles.brief: Original dark heroic tabletop-fantasy painting with anime-influenced character drawing. Deep cool colored shadows, focused warm ivory light, substantial cloth/metal/leather, selective sharp highlights, oil-like painted volume and soft lost edges. Preserve the subject's own canonical identity, species, anatomy, age, appearance and equipment. Use the approved K board for rendering style only; use that subject's own references for visual identity. No photographic skin, 3D rendering, copied franchise character or glossy merchandise finish. Character studies may use a deep charcoal ground; keep portrait faces readable. Environment and map lighting follow their actual scene and purpose rather than forcing darkness. Explicit user style choices override this default.

retained_styles.name: Severed Lands K: anime illustration
retained_styles.brief:
Draw original heroic fantasy characters with a clearly anime foundation and a controlled painted
finish. Use the supplied style image to judge drawing, edge control and shading. Each subject's
own references determine identity, age, species, build, complexion, hair and costume.

Faces: construct a deliberate stylized face with clean cheek/jaw silhouettes and readable eye
shapes. Give the upper eyelid a confident dark edge; design the iris, pupil and small catchlight
as graphic shapes. Make brows and mouth economical expressive marks. Describe the nose through
a small designed contour and broad light/shadow shapes. Keep the face recognizable through
shape and expression, with restrained surface detail.

Age and anatomy: retain the actual subject's age, proportions and distinctive features. Older
anime faces use mature silhouettes and a few intentional age lines; children retain their own
proportions. Scars keep their established side and shape. Species and creatures retain their
authored anatomy. The reference character's youth, face and body are never a template for others.

Hair: design large interlocking locks and ribbon-like groups with a clear silhouette. Use
selective interior lines, curved highlights and a few flyaways to explain those groups. Preserve
the subject's own cut, colour and hair texture; braids, curls and cropped hair remain distinct.

Shading: begin with broad, intentional shadow shapes that keep the drawing legible. Use controlled
soft transitions within those shapes to give painted depth; keep key facial and hair edges crisp.
Warm ivory key light and cool coloured shadows support the drawing. Keep skin smooth at normal
viewing size, with age marks chosen deliberately. Surface grain, pores, dirt and scratches are
secondary local details rather than a finish covering the entire face or costume.

Colour: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Pale linen reads
as pale linen; charcoal, plum, olive and auburn remain distinguishable under the same light.
Use coloured shadows and selective accents to keep dark fantasy readable. Restrict amber light
to illuminated planes instead of washing every material in a bronze filter. Never borrow the
style character's skin or hair colour to achieve the match.

Materials: explain cloth folds, leather seams and metal edges with selected shapes and highlights.
Place texture where it describes a particular material or authored wear. Ornament belongs to
the subject's established design. A cook's apron and a guard's practical uniform receive the same
careful illustration as a scholar's cape without gaining its embroidery, jewellery or silhouette.

Composition: give the subject a clear silhouette and character-appropriate expression. Keep
complete heads, hair and equipment inside usable margins. Portraits retain recognizable eyes,
face shape and expression at small UI sizes. Plain dark grounds suit reference studies; actual
environment and lighting follow the requested asset. The final image must retain the benchmark's
anime drawing even when its colour, age, species or clothing is very different.
